prayerExcerpt.en-US: How noble and heroic is this virtue of fortitude! how necessary for every Christian, especially for a pastor of souls, that neither worldly views nor fears may ever in the least warp his integrity or blind his judgment!
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Quão nobre e heroica é esta virtude da fortaleza! Quão necessária para todo cristão, especialmente para um pastor de almas, a fim de que nem as vistas mundanas nem os temores jamais desviem em coisa alguma a sua integridade ou cegem o seu juízo!

meta.face: A Frankish noble of about sixty-five, broad-shouldered and strongly built, with a fair, weathered complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face whose sides run nearly PARALLEL — a WIDE, FLAT, level forehead, a STRAIGHT, SQUARE jaw as wide as the brow, a long, straight nose ending in a BROAD, rounded tip, WIDE-SET, calm hazel eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT, dark-grey brows, a wide, firm mouth with a full lower lip; iron-grey hair cut short under the mitre and a SHORT, DENSE beard, dark-grey streaked with silver, trimmed close and square; the gaze level and composed. Not the broad, flat-planed, snub-nosed boniface, the short, curly-bearded denis, the white-haired, brow-ridged david_wales, or the lantern-jawed gregory_langres.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. His early biographers, as quoted by Wikipedia, call him a young man "of pleasing looks… well-built, strong, a good fighter"; the card keeps that strength in old age. The snow and the stone cross of Stavelot are the book's story (and its engraving).
